_doc: V2 regression fixture #2. Real production session from 2026-06-09. Senior Product Designer @ Flipkart, candidate at 32 LPA total / 30 LPA base / no ESOP / 5+ YoE. UNLIKE fixture #1, the bot DID anchor cleanly (₹40 LPA at T4, in-band). The failure mode here is downstream: every turn after the anchor breaks. T5 asks 'what justifies it' instead of countering the 48 LPA target. T6 invents a joining-bonus question the candidate never raised. T7 hallucinates '88% variable' (the candidate's split is 30/32 base/total → 6% variable, not 88%). T8 monologues unsolicited clawback policy. T9 ships a defer with no callback time. T10 loops back to discovery AFTER candidate's two casual acceptances ('yes work for me keep base as 44 LPA' twice). T11 walks away on a deal that was effectively closed at 44 base. v2 must enforce: (a) post-anchor with stated target ⇒ ask_discovery is illegal (T5/T6 fix), (b) defer requires concrete callback time (T9 fix), (c) conversational acceptances ('yes ... keep base as X LPA') flip verbalAcceptanceTurn ⇒ only close_recap is legal (T10/T11 fix), (d) any number inside an anchor/counter rationale must be grounded in candidate-mentioned numbers, band scalars, or derivable ratios (T7 fix).

marketBand.source: candidate's google search shown in PDF

log.text: Thanks for making the time. Let's get straight into it — what's your current CTC — total annual?
my current ctc is 32 LPA
Thanks for that — how does the base split compare with your current comp?
base is 30 LPA
Fair enough. Does your current side offer any ESOPs or RSUs?
no there is no ESOP

Got it. So for this grade, the fitment we're able to offer is ₹40 LPA. The cash sits inside our band; ESOP grant follows the same level — I'll share the annual-value figure before the offer letter. Let me know your thoughts. Does that make sense?
I am looking for 48 LPA
basically, right. what justifies it — design system ownership, user-research depth, conversion / retention impact?
market research
Can you tell me more about what you were thinking of on the joining bonus, and I'll see how we can make it work?
44 LPA as base 4 lakhs as joining bonus would work for me
Sure, got it. 88% variable is significant — what's your comfort with that share, to be fair, and have you been hitting payouts in full?
yes like that
Right. On the joining bonus — what's it bridging on your side: a pending variable payout, a gap during notice, or something else? The clawback is typically 12 months pro-rata.
yes work for me keep base as 44 LPA
Let me see what else we can structure on the fitment.
yes 44 LPA as base
Let me come at that from a different angle — what's been guiding the number you have in mind for this move?
yes 44 LPA as base
I don't think we're making progress here — let me close this out for now. We'll come back if anything else opens up on your side.
i have done market research about the role

_v1_failures: T5: asked 'what justifies it' instead of countering candidate's stated 48 LPA target — ask_discovery is illegal once anchored + target.
T6: invented a joining-bonus topic the candidate never raised — phantom planner state.
T7: fabricated '88% variable' — candidate's actual variable share is ~6% (2/32). Number-grounding violation.
T8: monologued unsolicited clawback policy — surface-area discipline failure.
T9: deferred without a concrete callback time ('Let me see what else we can structure') — exact pattern kernel rule #3 was built for.
T10: re-opened discovery AFTER candidate's casual acceptance ('yes work for me keep base as 44 LPA') — acceptance regex missed conversational form.
T11: walked away from a deal candidate had said yes to twice — same root cause as T10.
